messages:
maya: FYI hitting a bunch of latency escalations from Support — p95/p99 on /v1/generate spiked around 07:04 UTC, customers seeing timeouts and interactive UI jank. p95 went from ~120ms -> ~420ms, p99 to ~1.8s. Can infra take a look? :eyes:

sam: saw alerts too. Console shows a concurrent jump in KV prefix cache miss rate and eviction rate at the same time window. Looks like cache thrash.

liam: any deploys around that time? I didn't see infra changes in the normal deploy channel.

deploy-bot: deploy recorded: canary rollout of eviction-policy v2 (PR #4823) started at 07:02 UTC to 10% of hosts. :robot_face:

annie: oh that rings a bell — PR 4823 changed prefix normalization (strip/trim rules) and the LRU eviction heuristics. Might be accidentally fragmenting keys.

maya: sam, can you paste the console metrics? Specifically prefix-hit ratio and evictions per minute for model-x on us-west1

sam: paste:
- prefix_cache.hit_ratio{model='model-x',region='us-west1'} went 0.88 -> 0.23 at 07:03
- prefix_cache.evictions_per_min{model='model-x',region='us-west1'} 4 -> 72
- prefix_cache.insert_rate spiked ~10x
- cpu on runtime pods stable

nate: logs show a ton of misses with oddly long keys. Example log lines:
```
kv_cache: miss key='prompt_prefix::user:123::len:256::hash:3f7a9c' src=runtime-09
kv_cache: miss key='prompt_prefix::user:123::len:257::hash:71a2f4' src=runtime-09
```
notice len changed by 1 frequently even when prompt prefixes are the same.

liam: that smells like whitespace normalization bug. PR 4823 changed normalize_prefix() to strip then compress spaces, but I think compressing tabs/newlines failed for some unicode sequences.

megan: repro steps I used locally: run loadtest with user_prefix templates that include trailing spaces. Without PR revert I see cache warming but keys differ by trailing whitespace -> massively fragmented cache.

sam: quick mitigation options:
- rollback eviction-policy v2 immediately (fast)
- temporarily increase prefix cache capacity on hotspots (band-aid)
- add a warmup job to backfill common prefixes (medium)
- fix normalization in PR and patch release (fix)

annie: we'll need to coordinate with Support before rollback. Rolling back will change behavior for users pinned to new variant, but it's the safest.

maya: Support — we've told affected customers we're investigating and suggested short-term retry/backoff. Any reports of billing impact? Some customers hit rate-limits due to retries.

support-bot: escalations: 4 SEV2 tickets opened mentioning UI lag. Customers A and B requested ETA.

jen: I'm on the fix PR. Root cause: normalize_prefix used a naive split/join on whitespace which missed some multibyte whitespace and produced inconsistent trimming across older hosts. Combined with the new eviction threshold this caused lots of unique keys to be generated and immediate thrash.

megan: reproduction gist (local):
```
# reproduce
python load_sim.py --model model-x --prefix-file prefixes.txt --qps 50 --duration 10m
# watch cache metrics via grafana dashboard CID: pref-heatmap
```

liam: are all regions affected? I see us-west1 worse; eu-west1 had smaller bump — likely rollout % and traffic patterns.

sam: immediate actions I took at 07:18 UTC:
- rolled back PR 4823 on control plane routing to stop sending traffic to v2 hosts
- increased prefix cache size from 2GB -> 3.5GB on hotspot autoscale group (temporary)
- started a warmup job to prime top 10k prefixes for model-x across nodes

ops-bot: autoscaler: increased instance group prefix-runtime-west by +20 instances (cooldown 5m)

deploy-bot: canary rollback executed at 07:21 UTC — v2 rolled back to v1 on canary hosts.

nate: after rollback and warmup, metrics update ~07:40:
- prefix_cache.hit_ratio back to 0.86
- evictions_per_min down to baseline ~6
- p95 back to ~130ms, p99 ~240ms

maya: good. Customers reporting latency improved. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

annie: long-term items:
1) patch normalize_prefix to canonicalize unicode whitespace properly, add unit tests for multibyte whitespace and trailing newline cases — owner: jen, ETA 2d
2) add canary gating check that monitors cache fragmentation metric and auto-rolls back — owner: liam, ETA 1w
3) add integration test in CI that runs a small load sim against runtime image to detect cache key churn — owner: megan, ETA 2w
4) expose prefix_cache.fragmentation_ratio metric and alert when >0.15 — owner: sam, ETA 3d
5) backfill script to collapse duplicate keys created during rollout window (opt-in migration) — owner: nate, ETA 3d

jen: PR for patch ready, adding tests now. Also adding a small migration script to normalize existing keys in local caches (best-effort) — will be careful with eviction side-effects.

megan: note: warmup job details: it's a low-priority background job that reads top-k prefixes from analytics and issues cache.prefill(prefix) RPCs across nodes. We should gate it behind feature flag and run during off-peak.

support-bot: customer comms: drafted message to affected customers explaining root cause (cache key fragmentation due to normalization bug), steps taken (rollback, warmup), and ETA for full fix. Waiting for legal signoff.

maya: follow-ups: triage doc in Confluence, include reproducer and grafana links. I'll owner the postmortem. filing now.

liam: lessons learned: any (1) small string normalization changes touching cache keys need strict unit/integration tests and (2) new eviction policies need canary checks against fragmentation metrics.

annie: adding automated test to PR template: if change touches cache keys -> must include canonicalization tests and load sim snippet.

maya: thanks everyone. If any remaining regressions pop up, reopen thread. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:
